   130	  /// Warp boundary of a `BURST_WRAP` transfer (see A3-51).

   133	  /// The length of a `BURST_WRAP` has to be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.
   134	  function automatic largest_addr_t wrap_boundary (largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len);

   137	    // pragma translate_off
   138	    `ifndef VERILATOR
   139	      assume (len == len_t'(4'b1) || len == len_t'(4'b11) || len == len_t'(4'b111) ||

   145	    // In A3-51 the wrap boundary is defined as:
   146	    // `Wrap_Boundary = (INT(Start_Address / (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length))) ×
   147	    //    (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
   148	    // Whereas the aligned address is defined as:
   149	    // `Aligned_Address = (INT(Start_Address / Number_Bytes)) × Number_Bytes`
   150	    // This leads to the wrap boundary using the same calculation as the aligned address, difference
   151	    // being the additional dependency on the burst length. The addition in the case statement

   154	    // only allowed values for `len` of a `BURST_WRAP`.

   165	  /// Address of beat (see A3-51).
   166	  function automatic largest_addr_t
   167	  beat_addr(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst, shortint unsigned i_beat);
   168	    largest_addr_t ret_addr = addr;
   169	    largest_addr_t wrp_bond = '0;
   170	    if (burst == BURST_WRAP) begin
   171	      // do not trigger the function if there is no wrapping burst, to prevent assumptions firing
   172	      wrp_bond = wrap_boundary(addr, size, len);
   173	    end
   174	    if (i_beat != 0 && burst != BURST_FIXED) begin
   175	      // From A3-51:
   176	      // For an INCR burst, and for a WRAP burst for which the address has not wrapped, this
   177	      // equation determines the address of any transfer after the first transfer in a burst:
   178	      // `Address_N = Aligned_Address + (N – 1) × Number_Bytes` (N counts from 1 to len!)
   179	      ret_addr = aligned_addr(addr, size) + i_beat * num_bytes(size);
   180	      // From A3-51:
   181	      // For a WRAP burst, if Address_N = Wrap_Boundary + (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length), then:
   182	      // * Use this equation for the current transfer:
   183	      //     `Address_N = Wrap_Boundary`
   184	      // * Use this equation for any subsequent transfers:
   185	      //     `Address_N = Start_Address + ((N – 1) × Number_Bytes) – (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
   186	      // This means that the address calculation of a `BURST_WRAP` fundamentally works the same
   187	      // as for a `BURST_INC`, the difference is when the calculated address increments
   188	      // over the wrap threshold, the address wraps around by subtracting the accessed address
   189	      // space from the normal `BURST_INCR` address. The lower wrap boundary is equivalent to
   190	      // The wrap trigger condition minus the container size (`num_bytes(size) * (len + 1)`).
   191	      if (burst == BURST_WRAP && ret_addr >= wrp_bond + (num_bytes(size) * (largest_addr_t'(len) + 1))) begin
   192	        ret_addr = ret_addr - (num_bytes(size) * (largest_addr_t'(len) + 1));
   193	      end
   194	    end
   195	    return ret_addr;
   196	  endfunction

   282	  /// RESP precedence: DECERR > SLVERR > OKAY > EXOKAY.  This is not defined in the AXI standard but
   283	  /// depends on the implementation.  We consistently use the precedence above.  Rationale:
   284	  /// - EXOKAY means an exclusive access was successful, whereas OKAY means it was not.  Thus, if
   285	  ///   OKAY and EXOKAY are to be merged, OKAY precedes because the exclusive access was not fully
   286	  ///   successful.
   287	  /// - Both DECERR and SLVERR mean (part of) a transaction were unsuccessful, whereas OKAY means an
   288	  ///   entire transaction was successful.  Thus both DECERR and SLVERR precede OKAY.
   289	  /// - DECERR means (part of) a transactions could not be routed to a slave component, whereas
   290	  ///   SLVERR means the transaction reached a slave component but lead to an error condition there.
   291	  ///   Thus DECERR precedes SLVERR because DECERR happens earlier in the handling of a transaction.
   292	  function automatic resp_t resp_precedence(resp_t resp_a, resp_t resp_b);
   293	    unique case (resp_a)
   294	      RESP_OKAY: begin
   295	        // Any response except EXOKAY precedes OKAY.
   296	        if (resp_b == RESP_EXOKAY) begin
   297	          return resp_a;
   298	        end else begin
   299	          return resp_b;
   300	        end
   301	      end
   302	      RESP_EXOKAY: begin
   303	        // Any response precedes EXOKAY.
   304	        return resp_b;
   305	      end
   306	      RESP_SLVERR: begin
   307	        // Only DECERR precedes SLVERR.
   308	        if (resp_b == RESP_DECERR) begin
   309	          return resp_b;
   310	        end else begin
   311	          return resp_a;
   312	        end
   313	      end
   314	      RESP_DECERR: begin
   315	        // No response precedes DECERR.
   316	        return resp_a;
   317	      end
   318	    endcase
   319	  endfunction

    15	module fifo_v3 #(
    16	    parameter bit          FALL_THROUGH = 1'b0, // fifo is in fall-through mode
    17	    parameter int unsigned DATA_WIDTH   = 32,   // default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    18	    parameter int unsigned DEPTH        = 8,    // depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    19	    parameter type dtype                = logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0],
    20	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    21	    parameter int unsigned ADDR_DEPTH   = (DEPTH > 1) ? $clog2(DEPTH) : 1
    22	)(
    23	    input  logic  clk_i,            // Clock
    24	    input  logic  rst_ni,           // Asynchronous reset active low
    25	    input  logic  flush_i,          // flush the queue
    26	    input  logic  testmode_i,       // test_mode to bypass clock gating
    27	    // status flags
    28	    output logic  full_o,           // queue is full
    29	    output logic  empty_o,          // queue is empty
    30	    output logic  [ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] usage_o,  // fill pointer
    31	    // as long as the queue is not full we can push new data
    32	    input  dtype  data_i,           // data to push into the queue
    33	    input  logic  push_i,           // data is valid and can be pushed to the queue
    34	    // as long as the queue is not empty we can pop new elements
    35	    output dtype  data_o,           // output data
    36	    input  logic  pop_i             // pop head from queue
    37	);
    38	    // local parameter
    39	    // FIFO depth - handle the case of pass-through, synthesizer will do constant propagation
    40	    localparam int unsigned FifoDepth = (DEPTH > 0) ? DEPTH : 1;
    41	    // clock gating control
    42	    logic gate_clock;
    43	    // pointer to the read and write section of the queue
    44	    logic [ADDR_DEPTH - 1:0] read_pointer_n, read_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, write_pointer_q;
    45	    // keep a counter to keep track of the current queue status
    46	    // this integer will be truncated by the synthesis tool
    47	    logic [ADDR_DEPTH:0] status_cnt_n, status_cnt_q;
    48	    // actual memory
    49	    dtype [FifoDepth - 1:0] mem_n, mem_q;
    50	
    51	    assign usage_o = status_cnt_q[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0];
    52	
    53	    if (DEPTH == 0) begin : gen_pass_through
    54	        assign empty_o     = ~push_i;
    55	        assign full_o      = ~pop_i;
    56	    end else begin : gen_fifo
    57	        assign full_o       = (status_cnt_q == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH:0]);
    58	        assign empty_o      = (status_cnt_q == 0) & ~(FALL_THROUGH & push_i);
    59	    end
    60	    // status flags
    61	
    62	    // read and write queue logic
    63	    always_comb begin : read_write_comb
    64	        // default assignment
    65	        read_pointer_n  = read_pointer_q;
    66	        write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
    67	        status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q;
    68	        data_o          = (DEPTH == 0) ? data_i : mem_q[read_pointer_q];
    69	        mem_n           = mem_q;
    70	        gate_clock      = 1'b1;
    71	
    72	        // push a new element to the queue
    73	        if (push_i && ~full_o) begin
    74	            // push the data onto the queue
    75	            mem_n[write_pointer_q] = data_i;
    76	            // un-gate the clock, we want to write something
    77	            gate_clock = 1'b0;
    78	            // increment the write counter
    79	            // this is dead code when DEPTH is a power of two
    80	            if (write_pointer_q == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] - 1)
    81	                write_pointer_n = '0;
    82	            else
    83	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q + 1;
    84	            // increment the overall counter
    85	            status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q + 1;
    86	        end
    87	
    88	        if (pop_i && ~empty_o) begin
    89	            // read from the queue is a default assignment
    90	            // but increment the read pointer...
    91	            // this is dead code when DEPTH is a power of two
    92	            if (read_pointer_n == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] - 1)
    93	                read_pointer_n = '0;
    94	            else
    95	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q + 1;
    96	            // ... and decrement the overall count
    97	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q - 1;
    98	        end
    99	
   100	        // keep the count pointer stable if we push and pop at the same time
   101	        if (push_i && pop_i &&  ~full_o && ~empty_o)
   102	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q;
   103	
   104	        // FIFO is in pass through mode -> do not change the pointers
   105	        if (FALL_THROUGH && (status_cnt_q == 0) && push_i) begin
   106	            data_o = data_i;
   107	            if (pop_i) begin
   108	                status_cnt_n = status_cnt_q;
   109	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q;
   110	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
   111	            end
   112	        end
   113	    end
   114	
   115	    // sequential process
   116	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   117	        if(~rst_ni) begin
   118	            read_pointer_q  <= '0;
   119	            write_pointer_q <= '0;
   120	            status_cnt_q    <= '0;
   121	        end else begin
   122	            if (flush_i) begin
   123	                read_pointer_q  <= '0;
   124	                write_pointer_q <= '0;
   125	                status_cnt_q    <= '0;
   126	             end else begin
   127	                read_pointer_q  <= read_pointer_n;
   128	                write_pointer_q <= write_pointer_n;
   129	                status_cnt_q    <= status_cnt_n;
   130	            end
   131	        end
   132	    end
   133	
   134	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   135	        if(~rst_ni) begin
   136	            mem_q <= {FifoDepth{dtype'('0)}};
   137	        end else if (!gate_clock) begin
   138	            mem_q <= mem_n;
   139	        end
   140	    end
   141	
   142	`ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
   143	    `ASSERT_INIT(depth_0, DEPTH > 0, "DEPTH must be greater than 0.")
   144	
   145	    `ASSERT(full_write, full_o |-> ~push_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   146	            "Trying to push new data although the FIFO is full.")
   147	
   148	    `ASSERT(empty_read, empty_o |-> ~pop_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   149	            "Trying to pop data although the FIFO is empty.")
   150	`endif
   151	
   152	endmodule // fifo_v3
